full_answer:
### 1. Executive Summary / Direct Answer
I designed and built an enterprise-grade AI Customer Support Intelligence Platform powered by Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Multi-Context Prompting (MCP). Traditional RAG systems fail when customer queries span multiple documentation domains—such as diagnosing a printer hardware error and checking its warranty coverage simultaneously. [Source: AI Customer Support Intelligence Platform - Project Dossier.pdf, Page: 1, Chunk: doc_prod_4d6578a53efe_p1_c0000]

### 2. System Architecture & Components
   - **Presentation Layer (Frontend)**: React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Lucide icons, and Three.js 3D knowledge graph; features side-by-side mode comparison and live citation verification cards.
   - **Application Server (Backend)**: FastAPI (Python 3.13) high-throughput asynchronous REST API with strict Pydantic v2 schemas and modular endpoint routing.
   - **Hybrid Retrieval Pipeline**: Pairs dense vector search (ChromaDB with SentenceTransformers `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`) and sparse keyword search (BM25Okapi) fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF, k=60).
   - **Context & Safety Layer**: Multi-Context Prompting (MCP) partitions heterogeneous sources into partitioned blocks with prompt injection defense, token compaction, and citation validation.

### 3. Key Findings & Engineering Decisions
   - **Decoupled Model Architecture**: Supports remote inference (Mistral-7B via Colab) with instantaneous sub-10ms fallback to a local grounded synthesizer.
   - **Strict Storage Budget**: Maintains a 1024 MB maximum local footprint with Google Drive persistent backup.
   - **Zero-Hallucination Design**: Citation validator verifies exact source filenames, page numbers, and chunk IDs.

### 1. Executive Summary / Direct Answer
I designed and built an enterprise-grade AI Customer Support Intelligence Platform powered by Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Multi-Context Prompting (MCP). Traditional RAG systems fail when customer queries span multiple documentation domains—such as diagnosing a printer hardware error and checking its warranty coverage simultaneously. [Source: AI Customer Support Intelligence Platform - Project Dossier.pdf, Page: 1, Chunk: doc_prod_4d6578a53efe_p1_c0000]

### 2. Detailed Technical Explanation
   - **Citation Hallucination**: Foundation LLMs frequently construct persuasive answers while fabricating non-existent citation markers or misattributing claims to unrelated documents.
   - **Black-Box Retries**: End users and support agents lack visibility into why an answer was retrieved, which documents were consulted, or how retrieval modes compare against baseline implementations. The Solution: Multi-Context Prompting (MCP) Category Routing: Inquiries are classified into domain buckets (product_manual, troubleshooting, warranty, faq). Partitioned Budgets: Context windows are explicitly divided across categories to prevent mono-domain context starvation. Hybrid Fusion: Merges semantic vector rankings with exact lexical keyword match scores (BM25Okapi) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).
   - Q1: How does Multi-Context Prompting differ from standard LangChain or LlamaIndex RAG pipelines? Answer: Standard pipelines perform top-k nearest neighbor retrieval over a single flat vector index. In technical customer support, this produces “context dominance”—a long troubleshooting section will consume all k retrieved slots, starving warranty terms or user manuals. Multi-Context Prompting deconstructs queries into domain categories, runs targeted retrieval across segregated collections, and allocates fixed context budgets per domain before synthesis. Q2: Why use Reciprocal Rank Fusion instead of summing cosine similarity and BM25 scores? Answer: Cosine similarity is bounded between -1.0 and 1.0 (0.0 to 1.0 for normalized vectors), while BM25 produces unbounded positive values dependent on document collection statistics. ### 1. Executive Summary / Direct Answer
Q1: How does Multi-Context Prompting differ from standard LangChain or LlamaIndex RAG pipelines? Answer: Standard pipelines perform top-k nearest neighbor retrieval over a single flat vector index. [Source: AI Customer Support Intelligence Platform - Project Dossier.pdf, Page: 6, Chunk: doc_prod_4d6578a53efe_p6_c0000]

### 2. Key Technical Interview Questions & Answers
   - **Q1: How does Multi-Context Prompting solve context starvation?** Standard vector retrieval selects chunks strictly by global cosine similarity, allowing long troubleshooting passages to crowd out warranty terms. MCP partitions candidate chunks by domain and allocates context via round-robin balancing to guarantee cross-domain coverage.
   - **Q2: Why use Reciprocal Rank Fusion instead of score averaging?** Dense cosine distances and BM25 scores have fundamentally different distributions and scales. RRF operates purely on ordinal ranks ($1 / (k + \text{rank})$), eliminating calibration errors and score drift.
   - **Q3: How is zero-hallucination enforced?** CitationValidator cross-references all model claims against retrieved chunk IDs, verifying that source filenames, page numbers, and numerical values match ground truth evidence.

### 3. Core Engineering Decisions
   - **Decoupled Architecture**: High-speed offline local fallback guarantees 100% availability without external API costs.
   - **Google Drive First Policy**: Ensures ephemeral Colab and Windows environments operate under a strict 1024 MB local storage ceiling.

### 1. Executive Summary / Direct Answer
I designed and built an enterprise-grade AI Customer Support Intelligence Platform powered by Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Multi-Context Prompting (MCP). Traditional RAG systems fail when customer queries span multiple documentation domains—such as diagnosing a printer hardware error and checking its warranty coverage simultaneously. [Source: AI Customer Support Intelligence Platform - Project Dossier.pdf, Page: 1, Chunk: doc_prod_4d6578a53efe_p1_c0000]

### 2. Key Technical Interview Questions & Answers
   - **Q1: How does Multi-Context Prompting solve context starvation?** Standard vector retrieval selects chunks strictly by global cosine similarity, allowing long troubleshooting passages to crowd out warranty terms. MCP partitions candidate chunks by domain and allocates context via round-robin balancing to guarantee cross-domain coverage.
   - **Q2: Why use Reciprocal Rank Fusion instead of score averaging?** Dense cosine distances and BM25 scores have fundamentally different distributions and scales. RRF operates purely on ordinal ranks ($1 / (k + \text{rank})$), eliminating calibration errors and score drift.
   - **Q3: How is zero-hallucination enforced?** CitationValidator cross-references all model claims against retrieved chunk IDs, verifying that source filenames, page numbers, and numerical values match ground truth evidence.

### 3. Core Engineering Decisions
   - **Decoupled Architecture**: High-speed offline local fallback guarantees 100% availability without external API costs.
   - **Google Drive First Policy**: Ensures ephemeral Colab and Windows environments operate under a strict 1024 MB local storage ceiling.

### 1. Executive Summary / Direct Answer
I designed and built an enterprise-grade AI Customer Support Intelligence Platform powered by Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Multi-Context Prompting (MCP). Traditional RAG systems fail when customer queries span multiple documentation domains—such as diagnosing a printer hardware error and checking its warranty coverage simultaneously. [Source: AI Customer Support Intelligence Platform - Project Dossier.pdf, Page: 1, Chunk: doc_prod_4d6578a53efe_p1_c0000]

### 2. Detailed Technical Explanation
   - **Citation Hallucination**: Foundation LLMs frequently construct persuasive answers while fabricating non-existent citation markers or misattributing claims to unrelated documents.
   - **Black-Box Retries**: End users and support agents lack visibility into why an answer was retrieved, which documents were consulted, or how retrieval modes compare against baseline implementations. The Solution: Multi-Context Prompting (MCP) Category Routing: Inquiries are classified into domain buckets (product_manual, troubleshooting, warranty, faq). Partitioned Budgets: Context windows are explicitly divided across categories to prevent mono-domain context starvation. Hybrid Fusion: Merges semantic vector rankings with exact lexical keyword match scores (BM25Okapi) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).
   - Q1: How does Multi-Context Prompting differ from standard LangChain or LlamaIndex RAG pipelines? Answer: Standard pipelines perform top-k nearest neighbor retrieval over a single flat vector index. In technical customer support, this produces “context dominance”—a long troubleshooting section will consume all k retrieved slots, starving warranty terms or user manuals. Multi-Context Prompting deconstructs queries into domain categories, runs targeted retrieval across segregated collections, and allocates fixed context budgets per domain before synthesis. Q2: Why use Reciprocal Rank Fusion instead of summing cosine similarity and BM25 scores? Answer: Cosine similarity is bounded between -1.0 and 1.0 (0.0 to 1.0 for normalized vectors), while BM25 produces unbounded positive values dependent on document collection statistics. Direct linear combinations require manual
   - **Context Fragmentation & Dominance**: Support documentation is partitioned into distinct manuals (User Manuals, Troubleshooting Guides, Warranty Policies, and FAQs). For composite queries such as “My printer paper feed jammed during firmware update, is this covered under warranty?”, context is needed from three distinct sources. Standard vector retrieval selects chunks strictly by global cosine similarity, allowing long troubleshooting passages to crowd out warranty terms.

### 3. Key Findings & Important Details
   - **Evidence Grounding**: Statements are synthesized strictly from indexed document passages without speculative elaboration.
   - **Traceability**: All technical assertions reference exact source document names, page coordinates, and chunk identifiers.
